_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-15 directly to contract v3 per GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md (+ADDENDUM v3) and TEMPLATE-V3-PLAN-2026-08-15.md, using the Boston v3 files as structural exemplars. Sources: bay-area/REVENUE-STACK-BAY-AREA.md + bay-area/CREW-COST-BAY-AREA.md + bay-area/hub.json (geometry/catchment only). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields (_contract, _provenance, _internal, _guard) NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ LOCKED: utilization-stack economics lead frame. Upside rows are never summed into base totals. NOTE: fleet_phasing is intentionally ABSENT — no sourced per-line vessel counts exist for this city yet (no bay-area fleet-economics pass); section omitted rather than derived (fail closed). demand_pool renders as copy cards (cluster level) — hub.json carries no employer-headcount rows for this city; no named-employer table is authored.

fn1.text: Pricing and experience rates are benchmarked to Bay Area operators' and comparators' published 2025–26 fares.

fn2.text: Districts and clusters shown are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted speed and wake rules. Speed-rule relief appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base cases. Precedent: an electric hydrofoil exemption on Stockholm's Route 89.

fn5.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published San Francisco-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.

fn6.text: Spot-seat volumes are derived from each scenario's spare commute capacity at the stated fill rate (10–30%) and fare band ($35–55/leg); figures rounded to the nearest seat-leg.

fn7.text: The conservative case does not cover operating costs at Bay Area crew rates; the levers shown beside the P&L indicate what closes the gap.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day. Commuter bundles are the schedule spine; experiences, charters and spot seats buy down payback. Bay Area crew costs are carried here at full local rates — the levers below are what close the gap. Payback figures are for a single N45 Explorer (~$3M).

cards.title: Seat pricing headroom
cards.body: The mid case holds seats at $1,000 of an $800–1,200 band. Each $100 per seat-month across 48 seats adds ~~$4.8K/mo — roughly a year off payback.

cards.title: Experience pricing headroom
cards.body: The modeled $65 mid-case fare sits well below the Bay's $122–134 dinner-cruise tier — one of the deepest harbor-experience markets in the network.

cards.title: Crew-rate sensitivity
cards.body: Crew is modeled at $155/hr for a two-person crew, fully loaded. At the lower sourced rate of $130/hr, mid-case payback improves to ~6.6 yr.

revenue_rows.note: A discounted monthly pass — priced against a ~$60 door-to-door ride-hail trip and ~$340/mo downtown parking.

opex_rows.note: Electric operation across commute, midday, evening and weekend sailings.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.label: Energy
tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the 7-city network is the residual-value story.
